newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia needs protectionist import duties-minister.
newsitem.headline: Russia needs protectionist import duties-minister.

text.p: Russian Foreign Economic Relations Minister Oleg Davydov said on Tuesday that Moscow would use import tariffs to protect its domestic industries until they get back on their feet, Interfax news agency said.
"Changes to the scale of import tariffs will depend on the course of reform in the economy," he said.
"During the period of structural change, different sectors of industry will be protected from overseas competition through rises in import tariffs on the goods they produce," he added.
But he also said Russia's average import tariff, now 14-15 percent, would not rise and that Moscow hoped to lower those rates by 20 percent by 2000 and by 30 percent by 2005.
Russia is seeking membership of the World Trade Organisation.
Davydov, who is also a deputy prime minister and whose portfolio includes trade, named aviation as one sector in need of protectionist duties to compete against imports.
He made no mention of imported food, which comprises up to one half of the Russian food market.
Davydov and other government officials have beat the protectionist drum over the past 12 months and called for duties and curbs on imports.
But Davydov also said that excessive protection of Russia's automobile industry had contributed to disastrous production declines at some of Russia's major car manufacturers.
